proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the full affine-center local expected-length frontier, strict connectedness and mediator-margin comparisons, a stronger paired-rotation multiplier, and a published-class converse, then independently reviewed the proof graph and verified all eight cited leaves. Mathematics passed, but D0.5 graded the benchmark incremental (score ceiling 5.5) below the field floor; the actual optimal-length surcharge remains bounded only one-sided and useful numerical certificates are absent. Formalization and presentation were not launched; no Lean proof or substrate promotion is claimed, and future tier-moving work needs a materially stronger theorem or re-anchoring.
tldr: The principal result is a strict mediator-margin cost for connected 90 percent confidence intervals for a density-weighted pointwise principal risk difference in a public local sensitivity benchmark. An information-preserving rotation of the entire outcome-profile class inside that benchmark gives \(H_{\mathrm{conn}}(P,\kappa)\ge s_*(P,\kappa)H_{\mathrm{conn}}(P,0)\), with an identified sharp rotation factor, small-radius increment \(|\Delta|\kappa/50\), and an explicit saturation threshold. The previous conservative factor remains valid. Heterogeneous effects and positive radius imply strict cost; homogeneous effects give equality. A separate full-profile connectedness theorem proves \(H_{\mathrm{conn}}>H_{\mathrm{set}}\). Certified finite programs converge to the exact connected value, and uniform finite-policy transfer and a single data-only attaining sequence discharge the original-data frontier at scale \(n^{-2/5}\) across the full compact affine-center family \(\mathcal C^+\). Uniformly honest intervals on the larger specified-copula Zhang--Yang model must also pay this benchmark lower frontier, while exact equality and attainment remain specific to the benchmark. Zhang--Yang identification and fixed-bandwidth principal-effect influence functions, Armstrong--Koles\'ar confidence-set methods, and existing interval-program methods are credited ingredients. The fair design, affine centers and public prespecified \(\kappa\in[0,2]\) are bespoke benchmark restrictions. Zigler--Belin motivates the same principal-surrogacy question; no empirical fit, data transfer or trial recommendation is claimed.
gap: Zhang--Yang Theorem 1 identifies Cont.PCE under Assumptions 1--3, Theorem 3 gives Loc.PCE EIFs, and Theorem 5 gives fixed-bandwidth efficiency and inference. These results do not determine \(H_{\mathrm{conn}}(P,\kappa)\), the unsmoothed center-expected-length infimum over randomized connected intervals with coverage at every legal profile. Generic local-misspecification sensitivity bounds do not give the stated whole-class, heterogeneity-dependent isometric multiplier.
fill: The whole-class margin theorem and its observable-heterogeneity corollary supply the sole headline field claim. The PCE noncollinear-fiber lemma establishes the class-specific geometry for strict connectedness. Certified finite programs and the open uniform policy-transfer question tie the same \(H_{\mathrm{conn}}\) to inference in the stipulated sampling experiment.
